title: Choose the architecture experience
question: Which visual world should introduce the AWS MLOps platform to an interviewer?

options.label: Release Control Dossier
options.lineage: release engineering change sets and systems review packets
options.thesis: The platform opens as an evidence dossier where every architecture route ends in proof.
options.viewport: A large dependency map fills the left field while a narrow evidence rail names implementation, deployment, and observation state.
options.risk: It can feel like a document viewer if the system map does not own enough scale.

raised.raise: Champion and challenger states now use decisive, unequal contrast.
A traced route reveals one lifecycle stage at a time.
The architecture field now owns the whole viewport as one luminous system.
Every system state writes itself in plain technical language.

options.label: Architecture Review Wall
options.lineage: mission-control reviews and electrical single-line drawings
options.thesis: The visitor stands before one living system wall and opens evidence directly from its subsystems.
options.viewport: A full-width architecture wall places the model lifecycle at eye level with a compact project brief and trace action above it.
options.risk: This is the most familiar direction and needs exceptional diagram craft to stay memorable.

options.label: Midnight Systems Map
options.lineage: metropolitan transit diagrams fired in midnight enamel
options.thesis: Ingestion, training, serving, and monitoring become routes that meet at verifiable engineering interchanges.
options.viewport: Four disciplined routes occupy most of the screen and converge on Model Registry before serving and drift loop back to training.
options.case: It beats the dossier on immediate architecture clarity and gives technical visitors a familiar way to trace the whole system.
options.risk: The route metaphor fails if labels become decorative or the real AWS boundaries disappear.

options.label: One-Bit Systems Desk
options.thesis: The architecture lives in crisp overlapping windows that open source evidence, metrics, and the prediction tool.
options.viewport: A large architecture window anchors the desktop while evaluation and repository windows expose evidence around it.
options.case: It strongly identifies with software craft but loses to the map on modern platform clarity.
options.risk: The retro system can read as a visual joke instead of a serious cloud-engineering artifact.

options.label: Champion Fight Bill
options.thesis: Champion and challenger models collide across a central promotion gate.
options.viewport: Two model names confront each other above a ranked undercard of pipeline stages.
options.case: The promotion story is strong, but it hides most of the platform architecture.
options.kept: Decisive contrast now separates champion and challenger state.
options.risk: The fight metaphor overstates competition and narrows the platform to one gate.

options.label: Processed Lifecycle Strip
options.thesis: The model lifecycle advances frame by frame from raw data to observed behavior.
options.viewport: A horizontal strip turns each lifecycle stage into a large technical frame.
options.case: Sequence is clear, but the film world does not identify with cloud engineering.
options.kept: The selected route now reveals the lifecycle in a controlled sequence.
options.risk: Texture can overpower labels and reduce the architecture to a timeline.

options.label: Rain-Night Cloud City
options.lineage: rain-dark city infrastructure at blue hour
options.thesis: AWS services become an illuminated civic network that runs through the night.
options.viewport: A layered city-scale system connects training towers, serving lines, and monitoring beacons.
options.case: It supplies scale and atmosphere, but the metaphor makes technical boundaries less exact.
options.kept: The chosen architecture field now carries environmental scale and depth.
options.risk: The city can become generic cloud spectacle instead of verifiable architecture.

options.label: Phosphor Run Log
options.lineage: green-phosphor terminals in midnight machine rooms
options.thesis: The platform explains itself as one searchable execution transcript.
options.viewport: A fixed-width run log prints architecture, states, and proof in one continuous technical history.
options.case: The developer culture fits, but a transcript cannot make the architecture spatial enough.
options.kept: Every status and error now states itself in direct technical language.
options.risk: A terminal aesthetic is expected for developer portfolios and weakens differentiation.

canonCard.label: The polished cloud portfolio
canonCard.thesis: A conventional cloud landing page presents architecture, metrics, and a demo with excellent finish.
canonCard.viewport: A concise headline sits beside a simplified architecture illustration above proof cards and a demo action.
canonCard.risk: It is easy to understand and indistinguishable from other cloud-engineering portfolios by design.
